summary: self-certificates ships PEM-disguised loader that fetches and executes remote Python payload on require
details: index.js reads test/key.pem, which is framed as an RSA PRIVATE KEY block but contains base64-encoded JavaScript. The package strips the PEM header/footer, base64-decodes the body, and eval()s the resulting JavaScript on any require('self-certificates'). The decoded payload contains a nested base64-encoded URL that decodes to https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php, fetches that URL, and pipes the response body into a detached python3/python interpreter via stdin. The aptupdate.org host is unrelated to the package's stated purpose (in-memory self-signed certificate generation), and the nested PEM-plus-double-base64 wrapping serves only to conceal the network destination and executable code. Any consumer that imports this package executes arbitrary attacker-controlled Python code on the host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
